issues: What legal standard governs an immigration officer's obligation to consider the best interests of children affected by a humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) decision
Whether an H&C officer's failure to meaningfully analyze the best interests of children born in Canada renders the decision unreasonable
What degree of attentiveness, sensitivity, and responsiveness to a child's best interests is required in H&C decisions
Whether the decision is reviewable on judicial review for failing to properly consider a relevant factor
key_facts: Family applied to remain in Canada on humanitarian and compassionate grounds
The H&C application was refused by an immigration officer
The family has two children who were born in Canada
The officer's decision barely addressed the interests of the Canadian-born children
causes_of_action: Judicial review of an H&C decision under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act
Failure to consider best interests of the child as a relevant factor rendering decision unreasonable
candidate_statutes: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, section 25(1)
Convention on the Rights of the Child (as interpretive aid, not directly enforceable)
